qs.q: Why are some calligraphic pieces surrounded by decorated frames?
choices: To highlight the beauty of the writing
To mark the order of leaves in a volume
To indicate the date of copying
qs.why: Decorated frames and backgrounds enhance the beauty of a calligraphic piece.

qs.q: What shape is the measuring dot made by the pen nib in proportioned calligraphy?
qs.why: The full nib makes a diamond-shaped dot used to measure letters.

qs.q: Which of these scripts is one of the six classical pens?
qs.why: Naskh is one of the six pens whose rules were established in the calligraphic tradition.

qs.q: For what kind of writing was Diwani historically known?
qs.why: Diwani was associated with official correspondence in the Ottoman chancery.

qs.q: Which description fits the structure of Diwani letters?
qs.why: Diwani letters feature curves, close spacing and interlacing.

qs.q: Which feature helps make Ruqah quick to write?
qs.why: Ruqah reduces detail and abbreviates letters to make writing easier.

qs.q: Which script became widespread in book copying because it was clear and easy to read?
qs.why: Naskh was widely used for books because it suited texts intended for reading.

qs.q: Persian Nastaliq combines features from which two scripts?
qs.why: Nastaliq combines features of Naskh and Taliq.

qs.q: Which script was especially associated with writing Persian poetry?
qs.why: Nastaliq was a leading script for copying Persian poetry.

qs.q: What characterizes the decoration of floriated Kufic letters?
qs.why: Leaves and plant ornament intertwine with its letters.

qs.q: In which Kufic variation do letter extensions interlace like braids?
qs.why: Letter extensions form knots and interlaces in plaited Kufic.

qs.q: For what contribution to calligraphy was Ibn Muqla known?
qs.why: Ibn Muqla was known for setting geometric rules for the proportions of letters.

qs.q: Besides calligraphy, what administrative office did Ibn Muqla hold?
qs.why: Ibn Muqla served as a vizier in the Abbasid state.

qs.q: Ali ibn Hilal is the name of which famous calligrapher?
qs.why: Ali ibn Hilal is the calligrapher known as Ibn al-Bawwab.

qs.q: Besides calligraphy, in what artistic craft did Ibn al-Bawwab excel?
qs.why: Ibn al-Bawwab was a calligrapher and manuscript illuminator.

qs.q: Which city was the center of Yaqut al-Mustasimi's calligraphic activity?
qs.why: Yaqut al-Mustasimi's artistic activity was associated with Baghdad.

qs.q: For mastery of which script was Sultan Ali al-Mashhadi known?
qs.why: Sultan Ali al-Mashhadi was a major master of Nastaliq.

qs.q: Mir Imad al-Hasani was a leading master of which style?
qs.why: Mir Imad was known for his mastery of Persian Nastaliq.

qs.q: Why are silk fibers placed inside a calligrapher's inkwell?
qs.why: The fibers absorb ink and limit spilling during transport.

qs.q: How did a string ruling board help a scribe organize lines?
choices: By marks from small wheels on the surface
By a grid engraved in a metal plate
By leaving thread impressions beneath the paper
By ink lines drawn on the margin
qs.why: Paper is pressed onto taut strings, leaving guidelines for writing.

qs.q: What is the Turkish name for the paper-marbling art used to decorate calligraphic pieces?
qs.why: Ebru is the art of coloring paper with marbled patterns.

qs.q: How are traditional Ebru designs transferred to paper?
choices: From colors fired in a kiln
qs.why: The paper is laid on floating colors and picks up the pattern.

qs.q: Which shape underlies the construction of many stars and polygons in Islamic ornament?
qs.why: The circle and its divisions help generate geometric ornamental units.

qs.q: What plant form does the saz motif represent in Iznik ornament?
qs.why: The saz is an elongated ornamental leaf with serrated edges.

qs.q: In what direction did Ottoman garden-flower ornament develop in the sixteenth century?
qs.why: Depictions of flowers with features closer to actual garden flowers became widespread.

qs.q: How many points does the star have in the Islamic tile pattern known as star and cross?
qs.why: Eight-pointed stars alternate with cross-shaped tiles.

qs.q: How is writing arranged in the muthanna style of calligraphic composition?
qs.why: One calligraphic block reflects the other across an axis.

qs.q: When a traditional calligraphic piece combines Thuluth and Naskh, how do their sizes usually relate?
choices: Their sizes alternate in each line
Their letters are the same size
qs.why: Small Naskh is paired with larger Thuluth in this type of piece.

qs.q: Which master is associated with founding the Ottoman school of calligraphy?
qs.why: Shaykh Hamdullah was a prominent founder of the Ottoman calligraphic style.

qs.q: In which Gregorian century did Hafiz Osman, the Ottoman developer of Naskh and Thuluth, live?
qs.why: Hafiz Osman lived from 1642 to 1698.

qs.q: Which calligraphic tradition did Ahmed Karahisari continue to develop?
qs.why: Karahisari adopted Yaqut's traditions and refined them in his work.

qs.q: What is a muraqqa in the preservation of calligraphic models?
choices: A leather cover for a portable inkwell
qs.why: Selected calligraphic pieces are gathered and arranged in a muraqqa album.

qs.q: What does a student first practice in calligraphic exercises called mufradat?
qs.why: These exercises begin with isolated letters and then short combinations.

qs.q: How does an artist transfer a design to another sheet using pricking and pouncing?
choices: By immersing both sheets in colored water
By scraping the paper with a sharp tool
By passing charcoal dust through holes
By pressing the design between copper plates
qs.why: Charcoal dust follows the template's holes and leaves the design's outline on the paper.

qs.q: What color does lapis lazuli produce when preparing pigments for manuscript decoration?
qs.why: Lapis lazuli produces a blue pigment for manuscript decoration.

qs.q: In colored manuscript decoration, what color is malachite pigment?
qs.why: Malachite was used as a source of green pigment.

qs.q: What color does an artist use when decorating a manuscript with cinnabar pigment?
qs.why: Cinnabar is a source of red pigment used in manuscripts.

qs.q: Which craftsperson's name follows katabahu (written by) in the signature of a calligraphic piece?
qs.why: The phrase identifies the person who wrote the calligraphy.

qs.q: What practice underlies siyah mashq pages in Persian calligraphy?
choices: Repeating letters for practice and composition
Summarizing a theoretical work on calligraphy
qs.why: Letters and letter groups overlap to train the hand and build a visual rhythm.

qs.q: In art, what is meant by calligraphy?
qs.why: Calligraphy is the art of beautiful writing.

qs.q: How does Jali Thuluth mainly differ from ordinary Thuluth?
qs.why: Jali Thuluth letters are written larger than ordinary Thuluth letters.

qs.q: Which school is credited with developing the common Ruqah script?
qs.why: The Ottomans developed Ruqah.

qs.q: What does shikasta mean in Persian calligraphic terminology?
qs.why: Shikasta means broken.

qs.q: What contribution is attributed to Yaqut al-Mustasimi in calligraphic history?
qs.why: Yaqut al-Mustasimi contributed to the development of the six pens.

qs.q: Choose a component of traditional black calligraphy ink.
qs.why: Soot is a component of traditional black calligraphy ink.

qs.q: What is the function of the longitudinal slit in a reed-pen nib?
qs.why: The nib slit holds a quantity of ink.

qs.q: Why is gum arabic added to traditional ink?
qs.why: Gum arabic is a binder in ink.

qs.q: How does an ahar coating affect the interaction of calligraphy paper with ink?
choices: It gives ink a metallic sheen
qs.why: The ahar coating limits the paper's absorption of ink.

qs.q: What does an ijazah (authorization) from a calligraphy master certify?
qs.why: An ijazah (authorization) certifies the learner's competence to practice calligraphy.

qs.q: What subject appears in the miniatures of Nasuh Matrakci?
qs.why: Nasuh Matrakci painted miniatures of cities.

qs.q: How are spaces between Jali Diwani letters usually treated?
qs.why: Ornamental marks fill the spaces in Jali Diwani.

qs.q: Besides Persian, which language is widely written in Nastaliq?
qs.why: Nastaliq is widely used for writing Urdu.

qs.q: How do vertical and horizontal strokes relate in Nastaliq?
qs.why: Short vertical strokes and extended horizontal strokes characterize Nastaliq.

qs.q: Which calligrapher was known as the dean of Arabic calligraphy in Egypt?
qs.why: Sayyid Ibrahim was known as the dean of Arabic calligraphy.

qs.q: What is the body of the usual traditional calligraphy pen made from?
qs.why: The traditional calligraphy pen is made from reed.

qs.q: What tool does a calligrapher use to cut a reed-pen nib precisely?
qs.why: A fine knife is used to cut a reed-pen nib.

qs.q: What does a calligrapher's inkwell principally hold?
qs.why: An inkwell is a vessel for holding writing ink.

qs.q: Which material is used to prepare ahar coating for calligraphy paper?
qs.why: Starch is used to prepare ahar, the coating applied to calligraphy paper.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of passing a muhre tool over calligraphy paper?
qs.why: Passing a muhre tool over paper smooths its surface.

qs.q: How are letters made in the traditional qati technique?
qs.why: Letters are cut from paper and pasted onto another background.

qs.q: What underlies a student's training in traditional mashq practice?
choices: Copying texts in the student's usual hand
qs.why: Mashq practice is based on the student copying the master's models.

qs.q: Which artistic description fits an Ottoman tughra?
qs.why: A tughra is a sultanic signature with an ornate calligraphic composition.

qs.q: Which script did Mir Ali al-Tabrizi help codify?
qs.why: Mir Ali al-Tabrizi helped codify Nastaliq.

qs.q: Which two tools are used to construct traditional Islamic geometric ornament?
qs.why: Traditional geometric ornament is constructed with a compass and ruler.

qs.q: What is a qalamdan among traditional calligraphy equipment?
qs.why: A qalamdan is a case for storing pens.

qs.q: When a calligrapher uses kashida, what happens to the letters?
choices: Their edges are thickened by retracing
qs.why: Kashida is the extension of parts of letters in writing.

qs.q: In which script was Mustafa Raqim especially known for renewing the style?
qs.why: Mustafa Raqim was known for renewing Jali Thuluth.

qs.q: The decorative kundekari technique joins interlocking pieces of which material?
qs.why: Kundekari is based on interlocking wooden pieces.

qs.q: What makes up a calligrapher's portable divit?
qs.why: A divit combines a pen case and an inkwell.

qs.q: For mastery of which script was Ahmad al-Nayrizi especially known?
qs.why: Ahmad al-Nayrizi was known for his mastery of Naskh.

qs.q: Which calligrapher prepared the well-known workbook Qawaid al-Khatt al-Arabi?
qs.why: Hashim Muhammad al-Baghdadi prepared the workbook Qawaid al-Khatt al-Arabi.

qs.q: To which calligrapher is the book Ruh al-Khatt al-Arabi attributed?
qs.why: Kamil al-Baba wrote Ruh al-Khatt al-Arabi.

qs.q: Which metal does the zarandud technique use to render letters on calligraphic panels?
qs.why: Zarandud letters are executed in gold.

qs.q: Which stone is traditionally used to burnish gold in manuscript decoration?
qs.why: Polished agate is used to burnish gold applied to paper.

qs.q: In geometric ornament design, what is continuous tessellation?
choices: Covering a surface with units without gaps
qs.why: Continuous tessellation covers a surface with units without gaps.

qs.q: What is the artistic term for a radial medallion in Islamic manuscript decoration?
qs.why: A shamsa is a radial ornamental medallion.
